Variants.Content: The Order of Calatrava was the first Spanish military order of Castile, and it took its rule from the Cistercians. Its knights wore the red flory cross and held the fortress of Calatrava la Nueva in the Sierra Morena, the range that shields the Castilian plateau from Andalusia. From that position they could strike at Moorish columns before they reached the central plateau. Calatrava drew its brothers from frontier families who knew the passes, and it kept its garrisons supplied from estates along the Guadiana. The order's strength lay in combining monastic discipline with the skill of a frontier force that fought every season.

The Grand Master commanded dozens of commanderies and large flocks on the sheep pastures of Castile. Those estates paid for a corps of veteran heavy cavalry that stayed in readiness long after the feudal levies had gone home. A Castilian lord who wanted a share of the frontier wars had to deal with the order's treasurers as well as its captains.

Across sun-baked crags, Calatrava patrols ride in chainmail hauberks. Their arming swords are broad and heavy, and each rider carries the weight of a long day under the Sierra sun. Their task is to intercept the quick Moorish raiders who come north from Granada, so keep your horse fresh and watch the gaps between the rocks.
